lesson_title: The Bakkie That Quietly Gets Cheaper: Depreciation
hook_text: Your phone still works perfectly. So why is it worth half the price?
clip_script: Think of the newest phone you know. Launch day: full price, full pride. One year later — still working perfectly — try to sell it: two-thirds of the price, maybe less. Nothing broke. It just got older, and the world quietly marked it down. A business bakkie is the same story with bigger numbers: R120 000 new, worth less from its very first delivery. Should the books keep saying R120 000 for five years? That would be a polite lie — and books don't lie, even politely. So they tell the truth in three numbers: what it COST — written in ink, never changes. What it's LOST — growing every year. What it's still WORTH — the honest answer today. Receipt, wear, worth. And there are two honest ways to slice the loss: the same slice every year, or always a fifth of what's left. Which one fits a bakkie? Watch and find out.
visual_style: A gleaming bakkie aging through seasons in timelapse while three counters run beside it — COST frozen, WEAR climbing, WORTH falling; a loaf of bread being sliced two different ways as the methods appear.
mood: Wry, knowing, relatable — the truth everyone's phone already taught them.
pacing: Conversational open, steady three-number build, teasing close on the two slicing methods.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and slice the loss both ways yourself.
